subject: math
title: Factors, Multiples, Prime and Composite Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Factors and Multiples Worksheets: Factor Pairs, Divisibility Rules, Prime and Composite Numbers
standard_text: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 factors and multiples worksheets: find factor pairs with arrays, list all factors, use divisibility clues for 2, 3, 5, 6 and 9, tell prime from composite numbers, and solve word problems. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Factors multiply to make a number. Multiples are what you get when you count by it.
key_sub: 3 × 8 = 24: 3 and 8 are factors of 24, and 24 is a multiple of 3 and 8. A prime number has exactly 2 factors. 1 is neither prime nor composite, and 2 is the only even prime.
body_html:
Factors are the numbers you multiply

In 3 × 4 = 12, 3 and 4 are factors of 12. They are a factor pair. Every factor pair makes a rectangle of tiles. 12 tiles make 3 different rectangles, so 12 has 3 factor pairs.

Find every factor pair

Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. Stop when the pairs meet or turn around.

Example

Find all the factors of 36.

1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 5 is not a factor (36 ÷ 5 = 7 R 1). 6 × 6 is the middle, so stop and write 6 once.

Answer: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36

Multiples: count by the number

The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 … A number is a multiple of each of its factors: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 is a multiple of 6 and of 7. These clues tell you fast:

Multiple ofClueExample
2Ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 858
3Digits add up to a multiple of 387: 8 + 7 = 15
5Ends in 0 or 575
6Even and digits add up to a multiple of 372: 7 + 2 = 9
9Digits add up to 9 or 1881: 8 + 1 = 9
10Ends in 090

Prime or composite

A prime number has exactly 2 factors: 1 and itself. A composite number has more than 2. 1 is neither. To test a number up to 100, try 2, 3, 5 and 7.

Example

Is 91 prime or composite?

91 is odd, and 2, 3 and 5 are not factors. Try 7: 91 ÷ 7 = 13.

Answer: Composite, because 91 = 7 × 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing a pair: factors of 24 are 1, 2, 12, 24Test every number in order until the pairs meet: 3 × 8, 4 × 6
Mixing up factor and multiple: “42 is a factor of 6”The factor is the smaller number. 6 is a factor of 42; 42 is a multiple of 6
Calling 1 prime1 has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite
Thinking every odd number is prime (9, 51, 91)Check 3 and 7: 9 = 3 × 3, 51 = 3 × 17, 91 = 7 × 13
Thinking 2 is composite because it is even2 has only 1 and 2 as factors. It is the only even prime
Stopping at × 10: “84 is not a multiple of 6”Keep going past 10: 6 × 14 = 84

faq.q: How do you find all the factor pairs of a number?
faq.a: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order and write each pair, like 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6. Stop when the next pair would repeat one you have (6 × 4), so you know you found them all.

faq.q: What is the difference between a factor and a multiple?
faq.a: Factors are the numbers you multiply; the multiple is the answer. In 6 × 7 = 42, 6 and 7 are factors of 42, and 42 is a multiple of 6 and of 7.
No. A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is neither prime nor composite. 2 is the smallest prime and the only even one.

faq.q: How can a 4th grader tell if a number is prime?
faq.a: For a number up to 100, try dividing by 2, 3, 5 and 7. If none of them divides evenly, the number is prime. 91 looks prime, but 91 = 7 × 13, so it is composite.

items.q: 12 square tiles are in 3 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 3 × ? = 12
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 4. 3 rows of 4 make 12, so 3 and 4 are a factor pair of 12.

items.q: 16 square tiles are in 2 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 2 × ? = 16
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 8. 2 rows of 8 make 16, so 2 and 8 are a factor pair of 16.

items.q: 20 square tiles are in 4 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 4 × ? = 20
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 5. 4 rows of 5 make 20, so 4 and 5 are a factor pair of 20.

items.q: 18 square tiles are in 3 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 3 × ? = 18
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 6. 3 rows of 6 make 18, so 3 and 6 are a factor pair of 18.

items.q: 24 square tiles are in 4 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 4 × ? = 24
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 6. 4 rows of 6 make 24, so 4 and 6 are a factor pair of 24.

items.q: 30 square tiles are in 5 equal rows. Find the missing factor: 5 × ? = 30
items.e: Count the tiles in one row: 6. 5 rows of 6 make 30, so 5 and 6 are a factor pair of 30.

items.q: You have 12 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 12 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 2 × 6 to 6 × 2, does not make a new one.)
items.e: Each rectangle is a factor pair: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. That is 3 rectangles. Don’t forget the long 1 × 12 row.

items.q: You have 18 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 18 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 2 × 9 to 9 × 2, does not make a new one.)
items.e: Each rectangle is a factor pair: 1 × 18, 2 × 9, 3 × 6. That is 3 rectangles. Don’t forget the long 1 × 18 row.

items.q: You have 13 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 13 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 1 × 13 to 13 × 1, does not make a new one.)
items.e: 13 is a prime number. The only factor pair is 1 × 13, so you can make 1 rectangle: one long row. A single row still counts as a rectangle.

items.q: You have 16 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 16 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 2 × 8 to 8 × 2, does not make a new one.)
items.e: Each rectangle is a factor pair: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. That is 3 rectangles. Don’t forget the long 1 × 16 row, and count 4 × 4 only once.

items.q: You have 24 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 24 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 2 × 12 to 12 × 2, does not make a new one.)
items.e: Each rectangle is a factor pair: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6. That is 4 rectangles. Don’t forget the long 1 × 24 row.

items.q: You have 36 square tiles. How many different rectangles can you make with all 36 tiles? (Turning a rectangle, like 2 × 18 to 18 × 2, does not make a new one.)
items.e: Each rectangle is a factor pair: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. That is 5 rectangles. Don’t forget the long 1 × 36 row, and count 6 × 6 only once.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 28?
items.e: 4 × 7 = 28. 8 + 20 is also 28, but a factor pair must multiply to 28, not add to it.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 42?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42. 20 + 22 is also 42, but a factor pair must multiply to 42, not add to it.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 32?
items.e: 4 × 8 = 32. 16 + 16 is also 32, but a factor pair must multiply to 32, not add to it.

items.q: Which is a factor pair of 45?
items.e: 5 × 9 = 45. 20 + 25 is also 45, but a factor pair must multiply to 45, not add to it.

items.q: Mia lists the factor pairs of 24: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 4 × 6. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test each number in order: 1, 2, 3, 4 … 3 × 8 = 24 is missing. Turning a pair around (like 6 × 4) is not a new pair.

items.q: Owen lists the factor pairs of 36: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 6 × 6. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test each number in order: 1, 2, 3, 4 … 4 × 9 = 36 is missing. Turning a pair around (like 12 × 3) is not a new pair.

items.q: Zoe lists the factor pairs of 30: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 5 × 6. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test each number in order: 1, 2, 3, 4 … 3 × 10 = 30 is missing. Turning a pair around (like 6 × 5) is not a new pair.

items.q: Lily lists the factor pairs of 48: 1 × 48, 2 × 24, 3 × 16, 6 × 8. Which pair did she miss?
items.e: Test each number in order: 1, 2, 3, 4 … 4 × 12 = 48 is missing. Turning a pair around (like 8 × 6) is not a new pair.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 16?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 16, 2 × 8, 4 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Remember 1 and 16, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Remember 1 and 20, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 28?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 28, 2 × 14, 4 × 7. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. Remember 1 and 28, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Remember 1 and 30, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 32?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 32, 2 × 16, 4 × 8. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Remember 1 and 32, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 45?
items.e: Factor pairs: 1 × 45, 3 × 15, 5 × 9. So the factors are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. Remember 1 and 45, and keep testing until the pairs meet.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 36?
items.e: 36 ÷ 8 = 4 R 4, so 8 is not a factor of 36. The others divide evenly: 4 × 9 = 36, 9 × 4 = 36, 12 × 3 = 36.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 30?
items.e: 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2, so 4 is not a factor of 30. The others divide evenly: 3 × 10 = 30, 5 × 6 = 30, 6 × 5 = 30.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 48?
items.e: 48 ÷ 9 = 5 R 3, so 9 is not a factor of 48. The others divide evenly: 6 × 8 = 48, 8 × 6 = 48, 12 × 4 = 48.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 R 3, so 6 is not a factor of 45. The others divide evenly: 3 × 15 = 45, 5 × 9 = 45, 9 × 5 = 45.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 60?
items.e: 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4, so 8 is not a factor of 60. The others divide evenly: 4 × 15 = 60, 6 × 10 = 60, 12 × 5 = 60.

items.q: How many factors does 24 have?
items.e: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. That is 8 factors. Each pair gives 2 factors.

items.q: How many factors does 36 have?
items.e: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. That is 9 factors. Each pair gives 2 factors, but 6 × 6 gives only one: 6.

items.q: How many factors does 18 have?
items.e: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. That is 6 factors. Each pair gives 2 factors.

items.q: How many factors does 49 have?
items.e: The factors are 1, 7, 49. That is 3 factors. Each pair gives 2 factors, but 7 × 7 gives only one: 7.

items.q: How many factors does 50 have?
items.e: The factors are 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50. That is 6 factors. Each pair gives 2 factors.

items.q: 6 × 7 = 42. Which sentence is true?
items.e: 6 and 7 are factors of 42. 42 is a multiple of 6 and of 7. The bigger number, 42, is the multiple.

items.q: 8 × 9 = 72. Which sentence is true?
items.e: 8 and 9 are factors of 72. 72 is a multiple of 8 and of 9. The bigger number, 72, is the multiple.

items.q: 5 × 9 = 45. Which sentence is true?
items.e: 5 and 9 are factors of 45. 45 is a multiple of 5 and of 9. The bigger number, 45, is the multiple.

items.q: 4 × 8 = 32. Which sentence is true?
items.e: 4 and 8 are factors of 32. 32 is a multiple of 4 and of 8. The bigger number, 32, is the multiple.

items.q: Which list shows the first 5 multiples of 6?
items.e: Multiples of 6 are 6 × 1, 6 × 2, 6 × 3 … Count by 6s: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30. 1, 2, 3, 6 is the list of factors of 6, not multiples.

items.q: Which list shows the first 5 multiples of 7?
items.e: Multiples of 7 are 7 × 1, 7 × 2, 7 × 3 … Count by 7s: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. 1, 7 is the list of factors of 7, not multiples.

items.q: Which list shows the first 5 multiples of 8?
items.e: Multiples of 8 are 8 × 1, 8 × 2, 8 × 3 … Count by 8s: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. 1, 2, 4, 8 is the list of factors of 8, not multiples.

items.q: Which list shows the first 5 multiples of 9?
items.e: Multiples of 9 are 9 × 1, 9 × 2, 9 × 3 … Count by 9s: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45. 1, 3, 9 is the list of factors of 9, not multiples.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 3?
items.e: 3 × 19 = 57. The others leave a remainder: 43 ÷ 3 = 14 R 1, 73 ÷ 3 = 24 R 1, 52 ÷ 3 = 17 R 1. Clue for 3: the digits add up to a multiple of 3.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 4?
items.e: 4 × 19 = 76. The others leave a remainder: 54 ÷ 4 = 13 R 2, 34 ÷ 4 = 8 R 2, 42 ÷ 4 = 10 R 2. Clue for 4: the number is even, and half of it is still even.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 14 = 84. The others leave a remainder: 64 ÷ 6 = 10 R 4, 46 ÷ 6 = 7 R 4, 63 ÷ 6 = 10 R 3. Clue for 6: the number is even and its digits add up to a multiple of 3.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 8 = 72. The others leave a remainder: 39 ÷ 9 = 4 R 3, 29 ÷ 9 = 3 R 2, 98 ÷ 9 = 10 R 8. Clue for 9: the digits add up to 9 or 18.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?
items.e: 7 × 13 = 91. The others leave a remainder: 27 ÷ 7 = 3 R 6, 57 ÷ 7 = 8 R 1, 74 ÷ 7 = 10 R 4. There is no quick clue for 7, so divide.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 12 = 96. The others leave a remainder: 68 ÷ 8 = 8 R 4, 84 ÷ 8 = 10 R 4, 28 ÷ 8 = 3 R 4. Clue for 8: halve it three times. If you never get a remainder, it is a multiple of 8.

items.q: Is 87 a multiple of 3?
c: No. It does not end in 3
items.e: 8 + 7 = 15, and 15 is a multiple of 3, so 87 is too: 3 × 29 = 87. Odd numbers can be multiples of 3.

items.q: Is 75 a multiple of 5?
items.e: Numbers that end in 0 or 5 are multiples of 5. 5 × 15 = 75. Don’t stop at 5 × 10.

items.q: Is 92 a multiple of 6?
items.e: A multiple of 6 is even and its digits add up to a multiple of 3. 9 + 2 = 11, so 92 is not. 6 × 15 = 90 and 6 × 16 = 96.

items.q: Is 81 a multiple of 9?
c: No. It does not end in 9
items.e: 8 + 1 = 9, so 81 is a multiple of 9: 9 × 9 = 81. Odd numbers can be multiples of 9.

items.q: Is 70 a multiple of 4?
items.e: Half of 70 is 35, which is odd, so 70 is not a multiple of 4. 4 × 17 = 68 and 4 × 18 = 72.

items.q: Is 96 a multiple of 8?
c: No. It does not end in 8

items.q: How many multiples of 9 are there from 1 to 100?
items.e: 100 ÷ 9 = 11 R 1, so 9 × 11 = 99 is the biggest multiple of 9 up to 100. There are 11 multiples. Don’t stop at 9 × 10 = 90.

items.q: How many multiples of 7 are there from 1 to 100?
items.e: 100 ÷ 7 = 14 R 2, so 7 × 14 = 98 is the biggest multiple of 7 up to 100. There are 14 multiples. Don’t stop at 7 × 10 = 70.

items.q: How many multiples of 8 are there from 1 to 100?
items.e: 100 ÷ 8 = 12 R 4, so 8 × 12 = 96 is the biggest multiple of 8 up to 100. There are 12 multiples. Don’t stop at 8 × 10 = 80.

items.q: How many multiples of 6 are there from 1 to 100?
items.e: 100 ÷ 6 = 16 R 4, so 6 × 16 = 96 is the biggest multiple of 6 up to 100. There are 16 multiples. Don’t stop at 6 × 10 = 60.

items.q: Is 1 prime, composite or neither?
items.e: A prime number has exactly 2 factors. 1 has only one factor (1), so it is neither prime nor composite.

items.q: Is 2 prime, composite or neither?
items.e: 2 has exactly 2 factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime. It is the only even prime number.

items.q: Is 9 prime, composite or neither?
items.e: 9 has 3 factors: 1, 3 and 9. More than 2 factors means composite. Odd does not mean prime.

items.q: Is 31 prime, composite or neither?
items.e: 31 is not a multiple of 2, 3, 5 or 7, so its only factors are 1 and 31. It is prime. (3 × 11 = 33.)

items.q: Is 57 prime, composite or neither?
items.e: 5 + 7 = 12, a multiple of 3, so 3 is a factor: 3 × 19 = 57. 57 is composite.

items.q: Which number is prime?
items.e: 29 has only 2 factors: 1 and 29. The others: 27 = 3 × 9; 39 = 3 × 13; 1 is neither prime nor composite. Odd does not always mean prime.

items.q: Which number is prime?
items.e: 2 has only 2 factors: 1 and 2. The others: 1 is neither prime nor composite; 9 = 3 × 3; 21 = 3 × 7. 2 is the only even prime.

items.q: Which number is prime?
items.e: 53 has only 2 factors: 1 and 53. The others: 51 = 3 × 17; 57 = 3 × 19; 91 = 7 × 13. Odd does not always mean prime.

items.q: Which number is prime?
items.e: 89 has only 2 factors: 1 and 89. The others: 87 = 3 × 29; 81 = 9 × 9; 69 = 3 × 23. Odd does not always mean prime.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: 49 = 7 × 7, so 49 has more than 2 factors: it is composite. The others are prime, except 1, which is neither.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: 87 = 3 × 29, so 87 has more than 2 factors: it is composite. The others are prime.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: 39 = 3 × 13, so 39 has more than 2 factors: it is composite. The others are prime.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: 93 = 3 × 31, so 93 has more than 2 factors: it is composite. The others are prime, except 1, which is neither.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there from 1 to 10?
items.e: The primes are 2, 3, 5, 7. That is 4. 1 is not prime, and 2 is.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
items.e: The primes are 11, 13, 17, 19. That is 4. 15 = 3 × 5 is not prime.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 30?
items.e: The primes are 23, 29. That is 2. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9 are odd but not prime.

items.q: Grace says 51 is prime because it is odd. Is she right?
items.e: 5 + 1 = 6, so 3 is a factor: 51 = 3 × 17. 51 is composite. Many odd numbers are composite.

items.q: Maya says 91 is prime because 2, 3 and 5 are not factors. Is she right?
items.e: Also try 7: 91 ÷ 7 = 13. So 91 = 7 × 13 is composite. (9 × 11 = 99.)

items.q: Luis says 1 is a prime number. Is he right?
items.e: A prime number has exactly 2 factors. 1 has only one, so 1 is neither prime nor composite.

items.q: Emma says 2 is composite because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: 2 has exactly 2 factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime. Every other even number has 2 as a factor, so 2 is the only even prime.

sets.title: Word problems with factors and multiples

items.q: Ben puts 36 chairs in rows. Each row gets the same number, with none left over. Which number of rows will not work?
items.e: 36 ÷ 8 = 4 R 4, so 8 rows leave some chairs left over. The others are factors of 36: 4 × 9 = 36, 6 × 6 = 36, 9 × 4 = 36.

items.q: Nora puts 48 cupcakes on trays. Each tray gets the same number, with none left over. Which number of trays will not work?
items.e: 48 ÷ 9 = 5 R 3, so 9 trays leave some cupcakes left over. The others are factors of 48: 6 × 8 = 48, 8 × 6 = 48, 12 × 4 = 48.

items.q: Jack puts 40 stickers in rows. Each row gets the same number, with none left over. Which number of rows will not work?
items.e: 40 ÷ 6 = 6 R 4, so 6 rows leave some stickers left over. The others are factors of 40: 4 × 10 = 40, 5 × 8 = 40, 8 × 5 = 40.

items.q: Ava puts 60 photos in an album. Each page gets the same number, with none left over. Which number of pages will not work?
items.e: 60 ÷ 8 = 7 R 4, so 8 pages leave some photos left over. The others are factors of 60: 5 × 12 = 60, 12 × 5 = 60, 15 × 4 = 60.

items.q: Noah sets out 24 desks in rows. Each row has the same number of desks, and one long row is allowed. How many different numbers of rows can he use?
items.e: The number of rows must be a factor of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. That is 8 choices. Count both numbers in each pair: 2 rows of 12 is different from 12 rows of 2.

items.q: Kai sets out 18 chairs in rows. Each row has the same number of chairs, and one long row is allowed. How many different numbers of rows can he use?
items.e: The number of rows must be a factor of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. That is 6 choices. Count both numbers in each pair: 2 rows of 9 is different from 9 rows of 2.

items.q: Leo sets out 20 plants in rows. Each row has the same number of plants, and one long row is allowed. How many different numbers of rows can he use?
items.e: The number of rows must be a factor of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. That is 6 choices. Count both numbers in each pair: 2 rows of 10 is different from 10 rows of 2.

items.q: Pencils come in packs of 8. Sofia buys some packs. Which number of pencils could she have?
items.e: She can only have a multiple of 8: 8 × 7 = 56. 58 ends in 8, but 8 × 7 = 56 and 8 × 8 = 64.

items.q: Juice boxes come in packs of 6. Can Omar buy exactly 40 juice boxes?
c: No. 40 is not a multiple of 6
items.e: 6 × 6 = 36 and 6 × 7 = 42. 40 is between them, so it is not a multiple of 6. Being even is not enough.

items.q: Tennis balls come in cans of 3. Sam needs exactly 51 balls. Can he buy exactly 51?
items.e: 5 + 1 = 6, a multiple of 3, so 51 is a multiple of 3. 3 × 17 = 51, so he buys 17 cans.

items.q: Stickers come in sheets of 9. Ruby buys some sheets. How many stickers could she have?
items.e: 9 × 7 = 63, and 6 + 3 = 9. The digits of 69, 49 and 96 add up to 15, 13 and 15, so they are not multiples of 9. Ending in 9 is not the clue.

items.q: Cups come in packs of 6 and plates in packs of 8. Eli wants the same number of cups and plates. What is the smallest number of each he can buy?
items.e: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. 24 is the first number in both lists. 6 × 8 = 48 works too, but it is not the smallest.

items.q: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. Mia wants the same number of hot dogs and buns. What is the smallest number of each she can buy?
items.e: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40. 40 is the first number in both lists. 20 is a multiple of 10 but not of 8.

items.q: I am between 20 and 30. I am a multiple of 4 and a multiple of 6. What number am I?
items.e: Multiples of 4 between 20 and 30: 24, 28. Multiples of 6 between 20 and 30: 24. Only 24 is both. 30 is a multiple of 6, but not of 4.

items.q: I am a prime number between 30 and 40. My digits add up to 10. What number am I?
items.e: The primes between 30 and 40 are 31 and 37. 3 + 7 = 10, so the number is 37. 31 has digits that add up to 4.

items.q: I am an odd two-digit number less than 40. 9 is a factor of me. What number am I?
items.e: Two-digit multiples of 9 less than 40: 18, 27, 36. Only 27 is odd. 39 ends in 9, but 39 ÷ 9 = 4 R 3.

items.q: I am less than 40. 2, 3 and 5 are all factors of me. What number am I?
items.e: 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. 15 is odd, so 2 is not a factor. 10 does not have 3 as a factor, and 6 does not have 5.

items.q: I am an odd composite number between 50 and 60. 3 is not one of my factors. What number am I?
items.e: The odd numbers between 50 and 60 are 51, 53, 55, 57, 59. 51 = 3 × 17 and 57 = 3 × 19 have 3 as a factor. 53 and 59 are prime. 55 = 5 × 11.

items.q: Owen has 17 square tiles. Can he make a rectangle with all 17 tiles and more than one row?
items.e: 17 has only 2 factors, 1 and 17, so the only rectangle is 1 row of 17. 3 × 6 = 18 and 2 × 9 = 18, not 17.

items.q: This egg carton holds 12 eggs in 2 rows of 6. Which other carton could hold exactly 12 eggs in equal rows?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so 3 rows of 4 hold exactly 12 eggs. 3 × 5 = 15, 4 × 4 = 16 and 5 × 2 = 10.
